sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax for a Russell County house?
sections.html:
Four offices touch a Russell County tax bill. The PVA, reachable at (270) 343-4395, decides what each parcel is worth. The sheriff, at (270) 343-2191, collects payment. The clerk, at (270) 343-2125, inherits whatever is still open once the sheriff's season ends. The county attorney, at (270) 343-2121, sends the warning letters that precede the clerk's sale.

The fiscal court's own description of the PVA calls the office's valuations the basis of the bills that pay for local services. In plain terms, a complaint about the number goes to the PVA, and a question about where to send the check goes to the sheriff.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Russell County itself?
sections.html:
Russell County is a lake-and-ridge county in south central Kentucky. Lawmakers formed it on December 14, 1825 from pieces of Adair, Cumberland and Wayne counties. It spans 283 square miles, about 29 of them water. Jamestown holds the courthouse and Russell Springs is larger, at 2,715 people in 2020 against 1,867. The county was entirely rural in the 2020 census.

It runs on Central time, while Casey, Pulaski and Wayne counties along its eastern line use Eastern time. Keep that in mind when you line up a closing with an out-of-county buyer or title office.

  • Wolf Creek Dam, near the county's southern edge, backs up the Cumberland River into Lake Cumberland. Impoundment came in 1952, and the shoreline measures about 1,255 miles.
  • The Army Corps of Engineers began drawing the lake down in 2007 over seepage worries. A new wall inside the dam was done by early 2013, and normal levels returned in spring 2014.
  • Normal summer pool is about 723 feet above sea level, with the tree line near 725.
  • Voters approved alcohol sales on January 19, 2016, by 3,833 to 3,423.

If your home is near the water, expect questions about that drawdown history. The county also lists a surveyor among its elected offices, which helps when a shoreline boundary is unclear.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Russell County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey puts a typical Russell County owner-occupied home at $163,200. Median gross rent is $681 a month and median household income is $44,738 across 7,562 households. Owners occupy 70.8 percent of homes.

Vacancy is high by the 2020 count: 10,088 housing units, 26.0 percent empty. Builders pulled just 5 permits in 2025, so fresh construction is not crowding your listing.

  • July 1, 2025 estimate: 18,608 residents, a 3.4 percent gain over 2020.
  • People 65 and older: 22.6 percent of the population.
  • Average trip to work: 19.8 minutes.
  • Typical monthly owner costs: $1,219 with a mortgage, $341 without one.

sections.h2: When does Russell County tax come due, and what do late payers owe?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets one statewide calendar. A 2 percent discount applies to full payment by November 1. Until December 31 the printed amount is due. January adds 5 percent, and 10 percent applies from February 1 onward.

Per the clerk's page, bills are mailed in October and the sheriff keeps taking payments through April 15 of the next year. The statute also makes the tax a personal debt of whoever owned the property on January 1. That person's name is on the bill, so the sales contract should say who reimburses whom.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid Russell County bill after April 15?
sections.html:
The sheriff hands the unpaid bill to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien is recorded on the parcel. KRS 134.015 says that lien stays on the land through any change of owner. The clerk's page promises a tax sale before the end of August, with notice in the newspaper and on the clerk's site. Registered private buyers may purchase the certificate and then pursue the owner.

The clerk warns that the amounts on the delinquent list shift each month. Call before paying and ask for a current figure. The Department of Revenue illustrates the climb with a $1,000 bill.

Revenue Department worked example for a $1,000 Kentucky bill once the clerk holds it
When paidTotal in the example
Handed to the clerk (tax, 10% penalty, sheriff add-on and commission)$1,254.00
Within five business days$1,387.79
After the first attorney letter$1,611.30
Bought by a third party at the sale$1,704.21

Interest accrues at 1 percent a month on the certificate. Any buyer's title search will turn up the recorded lien, so plan to clear it before you close.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Russell County valuation?
sections.html:
Begin with the PVA. Law requires an informal conference first, and you can ask to do it by phone. Inspection of the roll opens the first Monday in May and runs 13 days. The conference must take place before that period ends.

Without a deal, put a written petition in the county clerk's hands by the workday after inspection closes. Name the parcel, give your reasons and state your own figure for fair cash value. The local board of assessment appeals then holds a hearing. Bring concrete evidence such as sale listings, building costs, income statements or loan papers. The appeal does not stop collection: KRS 133.120 has you pay on your claimed value and settle any difference, with interest, afterward.

sections.h2: Does Russell County have a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners 65 and over and for those classified as totally disabled. The state's figure was $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, and it comes off the assessed value before tax is computed. A house assessed at $200,000 would be taxed on $150,900.

The application goes to the Russell County PVA. Bring ID that shows your birth date. A disability claim needs a classification from a federal agency or a retirement system, and most claimants renew yearly. Service-connected disabled veterans and anyone ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems are exempt from the yearly renewal. The amount changes over time, so ask the PVA for the current assessment year's figure.

sections.h2: How is tax handled when a Russell County house sells?
sections.html:
Closing agents usually pull the current bill and any delinquent payoff, so request both early. A bill still open before April 15 sits with the sheriff, and after that date the clerk wants it, along with the extra charges in the table above.

Seasonal cabins, inherited homes and houses that fell several years behind deserve a written payoff from the clerk before you advertise them. A buyer who finds a lien in the title search will want it removed or will back out.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Russell County property tax payment?
faqs.a: To the sheriff's office, at (270) 343-2191, through April 15 of the year after the bill. Later payments for unpaid bills go to the county clerk's office at (270) 343-2125.

faqs.q: How much is the late charge on Russell County tax?
faqs.a: Five percent in January and ten percent from February 1, under KRS 134.015. Once the clerk holds the bill, 1 percent monthly interest plus clerk and county attorney fees pile on.

faqs.q: Does a Russell County tax lien survive a sale of the house?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 134.015 keeps the lien attached until the tax is paid or the 11-year limit in KRS 134.420 runs out, whoever owns the property. That is why title searches flag it.

faqs.q: What month is the Russell County tax sale?
faqs.a: The clerk must hold it before the end of August. Newspaper and website notices go out ahead of it, and the clerk's office at (270) 343-2125 can give you the date.

faqs.q: Do I have to apply for the Russell County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. Go to the PVA with proof of your age or disability status. The 2025 and 2026 amount was $49,100, and most disability claims renew every year.
